rationale: Both independently surface the same high-value, ground-truth-uncovered bug (double sample-rate conversion corrupting the WER number) with strong evidence, and both cover the audio_vae mutation, dropped language/dialect field, and the +2 decode-step change that the human thread discusses. X's top audio_vae finding fabricates a 'verified locally' experiment claiming the encoder actually executes only 4 layers at runtime, which directly contradicts the maintainer's confirmed resolution that the encoder's real layer count is unaffected — a serious grounding failure on one of its headline findings. Y frames the same issue accurately (stale config attribute / shared mutable object, not truncated execution) and backs nearly every claim with grep-verified evidence, plus catches a couple of additional real issues (stale 24kHz/mono WAV save path, cache-salt inconsistency) that X misses. Both are comparably actionable with concrete file/line fixes and test suggestions.
